quotes: we are going to keep these as fundamental programs

sourceScope: #548/#85 provide fundamentals and interlocking-program context. Counting calendar training days consistently with existing days-per-week capacity is a Strength Lab accounting repair, not a new Wildman frequency prescription.
behavior: Core recurrence demand is measured between distinct physical core training days; duplicate same-day movement receipts cannot inflate visit distance or replace a real interval with zero.

Reservation attendance uses distinct selected training days. A day containing real core work receives one core attendance credit even when another selected program is also recorded that day; same-day record order cannot remove it.
All actual receipts, stable identities, sets, loads, method histories and earned progression remain intact. Two genuine completed same-day exposures still retain their existing progression meaning.

Partial actual work consumes its existing physical-day opportunity without earning progression. Empty/no-actual work does not create attendance. Date correction/undo and future evidence boundaries recompute capacity from actual history.
Projection bookkeeping retains one entry per future opportunity; no forecast is converted into actual attendance. No new state field, setting, migration or source numerical protocol is introduced.

longitudinal.scope: Two years with a missed month, readiness reductions, partials, same-day extra work and developing practice; actual prescriptions recorded explicitly, not proof that the generator selected these historical sessions.

limits: This removes false overload caused by record segmentation; genuinely oversized curricula and movement-specific maintenance frequencies remain unresolved.
Other ordering heuristics may still distinguish separate workout records; only capacity and earned-work invariants are claimed.
No physical technique, retention outcome or Android hardware acceptance is certified. All ten gate areas remain unresolved.
testingNote: The hand-change browser test installs its virtual clock before the pause target so transport latency cannot request a pause in the past; all original timer/progression assertions remain.
